title: Dataset manifest (SIH26104 / PS104)
description:
The versioned record of every audio file used to train, calibrate, or evaluate the detector. Normative for column names and types in ALL serialisations: the playbook (PS104_AI_Training_and_Evaluation_Playbook.md 2.1) stores the manifest as manifest.parquet or manifest.csv, and the writer for those formats must derive its header from this schema rather than from a separate list. JSON is the validation form because a schema can be enforced on it in CI.

THERE IS NO AUDIO PATH FIELD, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Section 2.1 keeps the raw recording path in controlled research storage; audit and deployment data never receive it. Resolution from sample_id to a local file is done by a side-car map that is NOT in version control and is NOT validated by this schema, so a manifest can be committed, reviewed, and shipped without ever carrying a pointer to a waveform (rules.md R-14, R-15). The property set is closed (additionalProperties: false) at every level, so adding audio_path, waveform_uri, pcm_blob, transcript, or embedding is a schema change with a reviewer attached, not a convenience.

The grouping block is the reason this schema exists rather than a README convention. See $defs.grouping.

schema_version.description: Pinned. A manifest that does not declare the schema version it was written against cannot be validated years later, when the schema has moved and the manifest has not.

manifest_id.description: Stable identifier for THIS manifest, cited by every calibration artifact, model card, and evaluation report produced from it. calibration.json's fit.manifest_sha256 pairs a fitted mapping with the exact manifest it was fitted on; without that pair, a reported number cannot be reproduced.

source_snapshot.description: Upstream corpora move. MLAAD and IndicVoices are both explicitly required to be pinned to an exact release (playbook 2), because 'we used MLAAD' does not identify a dataset.

access_terms_accepted_by.description: A person, not a team. IndicVoices access terms are accepted by somebody, and licence compliance with no named acceptor is nobody's job.

identifier.description: A slug, not free text. Bounded so a note, a stack trace, or a person's name cannot be parked in one.

sha256.description: 64 lowercase hex, the same shape the audit table's CHECK constraints enforce.

record.description: One audio file, once. The closed property set is a privacy control: every field here was reviewed, and there is no place to attach an unreviewed one.

sample_id.description: Stable, immutable key. Immutable matters: it is cited by the consent ledger, by every split assignment, and by derived_from_sample_id on augmented children.

split.description: Playbook 2.2. Enumerated so a typo cannot invent a split: 'eval-locked' silently becoming an unrecognised value is how a locked hold-out leaks into tuning without anyone editing a line of splitting code. dev_calibration is the ONLY split a calibrator or a threshold may be fitted on (rules.md R-37); eval_locked is opened once, for the final report, per candidate release.

label.description: Training target ONLY. Never rendered to a user and never written to the audit table: the deployed system reports a risk score and a proportionate action, not a verdict (rules.md R-07).

source_license.description: Per record, not per manifest. A mixed manifest under one declared licence is a compliance claim nobody can substantiate.

speaker_id_hash.description: Namespace-salted SHA-256 of the upstream speaker identifier. A hash, so speaker-disjoint splitting is possible without the manifest holding an identity; salted with a project namespace, so the same speaker cannot be re-identified by hashing a guessed id from another corpus.

language.description: BCP 47, e.g. hi, bn, en-IN. Required for the codec-language cohort report; a manifest without it cannot answer 'does this work in Bengali on a mid-range Android'.

script.description: ISO 15924 four-letter code: Deva, Beng, Latn, Taml. A code rather than a name ('Devanagari') because two spellings of one script split a cohort in half and halve its apparent sample count.

accent_region.description: Controlled vocabulary or the literal 'unknown'. Used for bias analysis, which is the one thing it is for.

accent_region_source.description: NEVER INFERRED FROM AUDIO (playbook 2.1). The enum deliberately has no value for it: a pipeline that classified accent from the waveform could not describe what it did and still validate. Inferring a speaker's region from their voice and then using it for bias analysis measures the inference, not the bias, and it builds a demographic classifier nobody asked for.

generator_family.description: VITS, YourTTS, xtts, none. 'none' for bona fide speech — explicit, never blank, because a blank is indistinguishable from a field the pipeline forgot to fill.

generator_version.description: Family alone is not enough for a generator-disjoint split: two versions of one family can be as different as two families, and holding out only the family lets a version leak.

attack_type.description: Failure analysis. Reporting one pooled EER across attack types hides which attack the detector cannot see.

codec.description: The FULL chain as one token where it matters, e.g. opus_24k_then_g711. A codec column that records only the last transcode cannot explain a cohort's degradation.

sample_rate_hz.description: The deployed pipeline is 16 kHz mono. Everything else must be resampled with the recipe recorded, and an 8 kHz telephony sample upsampled to 16 kHz is NOT the same as native 16 kHz — the manifest has to keep the distinction so the cohort report can too.

channel_condition.description: Robustness stratification. 'unknown' is permitted and is not the same as 'clean'; treating unlabelled data as clean is how a robustness claim gets made about data nobody characterised.

duration_ms.description: Deduplication and eligibility. A sample shorter than the model's input window cannot produce an eligible window at all, and counting it in a split's size overstates the evidence.

sha256_audio.description: Content hash of the audio bytes. Two purposes: cross-split duplicate detection (the same file under two sample_ids in train and eval_locked is the most direct possible leak), and reproducibility of a reported number. It is a hash, not a path — it identifies the content without locating it.

consent_basis.description: Mandatory on EVERY record, not only local data. A public corpus carries public-corpus-license-only, which is an explicit statement that the legal basis is the licence and there is no individual consent — different from an empty field, which is an absence of information. Anything else must have a matching record in datasets/consent_ledger/.

retention_expiry.description: The date after which this sample must not be retained. Null is permitted ONLY with public-corpus-license-only (enforced by the if/then below), because a corpus governed by a licence has no consent clock to expire. For every other basis a date is mandatory: consent without an expiry is indefinite consent, which is not what anyone signs.

derived_from_sample_id.description: The IMMEDIATE parent for an augmented sample; null for an original. Immediate, so the chain is reconstructible — and NOT the field to group a split on. See grouping.root_sample_id for why.

notes.description: Bounded free text for dataset provenance oddities. Bounded because an unbounded note field on a per-speaker record becomes a place someone writes a name.

allOf.$comment: An augmented sample must declare a depth of at least 1. A child that claims depth 0 would be grouped as its own root and could land in a different split from its parent.

And the converse: depth 0 means there is no parent. Without this, a record could declare depth 0 while naming a parent, which reads as 'grouped as an original' and 'derived from something' at the same time.
Only a licence-governed public corpus may omit a retention date.
Bona fide speech is never labelled as generated. Playbook 2: never label natural speech itself as spoof.
A spoof sample with no named generator cannot be held out by generator, which makes the future-TTS split unenforceable for it.

grouping.description:
THE SPLIT GROUPING, STATED PER RECORD RATHER THAN ASSUMED.

Playbook 2.2 requires grouping BEFORE any augmentation, disjoint by speaker, parent sample, session, and generator family/version. That requirement is normally satisfied by a splitting script and documented in prose, which means the manifest carries no evidence that it was honoured — and a manifest that was grouped wrongly looks exactly like one that was grouped correctly. This block is what makes the difference visible: every record states which keys it was grouped on and the composite key it landed in, so the disjointness claim is checkable from the manifest alone by scripts/validate_manifest.py.

The leak this prevents, concretely: augment first, split second, and a speaker's clean sample lands in train while its noise-augmented child lands in eval_locked. Every reported number is then measured on data the model trained on, the split protocol was followed to the letter, and the result is meaningless.

grouped_before_augmentation.description: A const, not a boolean. There is no valid manifest in which this is false, so the schema does not offer the option — a pipeline that augmented before grouping cannot produce a valid manifest and describe itself honestly at the same time. This is a declaration and not a proof; the proof is grouping_key_sha256 being disjoint across splits, which is a cross-record check and therefore the validator's job.

group_by.description: The exact keys the splitter grouped on, pinned as a const so a splitter that grouped on speaker alone produces an invalid manifest. Listing them makes the grouping explicit rather than implied: a reader of one record can see what disjointness was enforced without reading the splitting code.

root_sample_id.description:
The ROOT of the derivation chain — not derived_from_sample_id. For an original, this equals sample_id.

The distinction is the whole point. In a chain A -> B -> C, grouping on the immediate parent puts B in A's group and C in B's group, so A and C are in DIFFERENT groups and may be split apart. Grouping on the root keeps all three together. Two-step augmentation (resample, then codec) is routine, so this is not a hypothetical.

generator_group_id.description: family:version for spoof, the literal 'bonafide' for genuine speech. Family alone would let a held-out version leak; a null would drop bona fide records out of the grouping entirely and let a speaker's genuine audio cross the split their spoofed audio was held out of.

augmentation_depth.description: 0 for an original. Bounded: a depth beyond a handful means the chain to the root is long enough that a single broken link somewhere in it has silently changed which group the sample belongs to.

grouping_key_sha256.description:
sha256 of the three group_by values joined by 0x1f (unit separator), in group_by order. The composite group this record belongs to, precomputed so disjointness is a GROUP BY over one column instead of a re-derivation nobody re-runs.

THE INVARIANT scripts/validate_manifest.py MUST CHECK: no grouping_key_sha256 value may appear under more than one split. That single check is the split protocol. A separator that cannot occur inside any of the three values is used so that ('a', 'bc') and ('ab', 'c') cannot collide into one key.
